summary: On a Mars mission, a doctor's reply can take up to 44 minutes round trip. HALO is an offline-first health co-pilot that lets astronauts, who are not doctors, measure, understand and act on their own health. It measures heart rate with a phone camera, runs NASA-style fatigue and vision self-tests, and judges every reading against clinical ranges and the astronaut's own baseline, explaining each flag in plain language. Results appear on a digital twin, including an orbitable 3D anatomical hologram. A voice assistant logs readings, answers questions and opens the right check. In an emergency, HALO becomes a voice-guided coach (CPR metronome, microgravity CPR positions, chest-pain triage) and sends an SBAR handover report to a simulated flight surgeon with a real light-time delay. The same tool could serve remote communities on Earth with limited access to doctors.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

- Bridge + Digital Twin: clickable body systems (brain, eyes, heart, lungs, blood, bones, radiation) showing status as colour + icon + word, how spaceflight affects each system, and what to do. A 3D anatomical hologram can be rotated and zoomed.

- Camera heart rate: fingertip photoplethysmography (band-pass filter, FFT, signal-quality gate). If signal quality is poor, HALO shows no reading rather than guessing. A contactless face mode is included as experimental.

- Guided checks: blood pressure, SpO2, temperature, glucose, breathing rate, sleep, mood, each with "how to measure / why it matters in space / what to do".

- Personal baselines: every value is judged against clinical ranges AND the astronaut's own baseline, with a plain-English reason for each flag. Rules are deterministic and explainable; no black-box model decides health status.

- PVT-B reaction test and Amsler grid vision self-check.

- Readiness score with a visible breakdown; scheduled checks, reminders and adherence streaks.

- Radiation dose tracking against the career limit, with a solar-storm shelter protocol.

- HALO voice assistant: speak or type to log readings ("blood pressure 128 over 82"), report symptoms ("my vision is blurry"), ask questions, or read messages from Earth.

- Emergency mode: voice-guided, captioned protocols (CPR coach with 110/min metronome and microgravity positions, chest pain, toxic atmosphere, radiation storm), a decision clock showing the earliest possible answer from Earth, and an auto-generated SBAR report.

- Ground Link: alerts travel to a simulated flight-surgeon console with light-time delay; replies return the same way.

- Environments: space station, Mars transit, Moon base, Mars base, rover. Each changes gravity, delay, radiation rate and available equipment.

- Judge Mode: a 90-second narrated tour on the landing page.

HOW IT WORKS

A progressive web app; health features run on the device with no server. Data is stored locally (IndexedDB). 120+ automated tests cover thresholds, baseline logic, signal processing, test scoring and emergency logic.

TOOLS

TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Dexie, three.js / react-three-fiber, MediaPipe Tasks Vision, Web Speech API, Vitest. Hosted on Vercel.

Code: https://github.com/meowhuriya/halo

LIMITS

HALO is a prototype, not a medical device. Demo-mission data is simulated and labelled. Voice answers use the browser's speech recognition (Chrome/Edge); buttons and typing always work.
